severity_standard: Demonstrated invalid derivation tied to a core contribution or demonstrated material core-claim damage supports Major. No whole-paper refutation, empirical-score deterioration, hard-repair condition or Major quota is imposed.

findings.title: Theorem 4.8/D.5 fails for allowed Lipschitz activations
findings.claim: Output difference is controlled by coefficient-weighted or summed-depth modified tree distances under merely Lipschitz activations/readout.

assumptions_verified: No equal-size restriction; blank padding explicitly defined
Weights norm 1; Lipschitz maps meet all stated assumptions
counterexample.stated: All TMD depths 1,2,3 equal 0, hence both stated upper bounds equal 0

findings.proof_failure: Eq. (20) transfers unequal ancestor-degree scaling through a nonlinear F using Lipschitz continuity alone. |F(0)/1-F(0)/2|=c/2>0 while the corresponding scaled raw input difference is 0.
alternative_readings: Eq. (18) identity may be justified by zero padding transformed embeddings and is not itself alleged invalid.
Primary all-zero witness does not depend on inherited-versus-reset degree convention.
Implementations using narrower activations are not shown empirically defective.
findings.dependency: D.5 -> main 4.8 -> coefficient-dependent Lipschitz constant used in 4.9 -> core inductive generalization interpretation.
findings.what_survives: Other perturbation bounds, localization observations and restricted architectures are not refuted.

repair_verification.detail: Zero-preservation alone is insufficient for coefficient-weighted D.5 under inherited degrees, as the scoped clipped-activation diagnostic shows; diagnostic does not refute the main summed-depth bound.

findings.title: Theorem 4.9 fails for the stated arbitrary nonnegative loss
findings.claim: Target risk <= source risk + 2 K_Lip W1 + best joint risk for the stated nonnegative-loss setup.

counterexample.hypothesis_class: h_a(P)=aP^2, a in [0,1], identity activation/readout, W1=W2=1
counterexample.uniform_constant: K_Lip=1 independently valid for the entire class over all K2 scalar features in [0,5/2]; each depth distance equals d_OT and output differences <=d_OT<=3d_OT
assumptions_verified: Same labeling function in both domains
Evaluated filter has genuine degree 2; strict positive a gives same infimum if required

findings.proof_failure: Absolute-disagreement triangle/Lipschitz argument imported from Shen et al. does not apply to arbitrary nonnegative loss with the same coefficient.
findings.counterevidence: Shen v4 p.5 assumes [0,1]-valued hypotheses, absolute disagreement, shared labels and a common class Lipschitz constant. Its own result is not refuted. Separate transductive softmax does not restrict Eq. (6).
findings.dependency: Core stability-to-out-of-domain-risk conversion in Section 4.3; independent of P1 because a common constant is separately proven.
findings.what_survives: Original cited result within its own assumptions and the empirical figures.

repair_verification.detail: Loss/class restrictions and constants require derivation with valid stability.

findings.title: F.6 radius-only bound eliminates genuine sampling fluctuation
findings.claim: High-probability transductive gap bound proportional to radius R on the stated closed parameter ball.

assumptions_verified: Closed ball nonempty at R=0; no lower radius bound stated
counterexample.actual: Gap +1 or -1 each probability 1/2; L1=sqrt(14), L2=10, claimed RHS=0; fails delta=1/4.

findings.extended_check: For every odd m>=3 use C_(2m), constant predictor and balanced labels: gap=(2J-m)/m, J hypergeometric(2m,m,m), P(gap>0)=1/2. A positive-radius R=1/m observation is explicitly conditional on uniform big-O dependence.
findings.original_source: Tang-Liu p.3 uses open ball r>=1; Proposition4.15 gives loss constants; p.22 Eq.(28) retains radius-independent sampling terms. Its theorem is not refuted.
findings.dependency: F.6 is the technical transductive guarantee invoked in main Section 4.3 for the complexity/generalization position.
findings.what_survives: No claim that trained model scores deteriorate; positive perturbation results remain.

repair_verification.detail: Reconstruct radius scope, sampling terms and probability statement.

findings.title: The asserted exact-k nodal-domain existence is false
findings.claim: At least one eigenvector at lambda_k has exactly k nodal domains.
findings.counterexample: Connected unweighted K3 has normalized spectrum (0,3/2,3/2); every nonzero lambda_3 vector has zero sum and exactly two maximal strong or weak sign domains, never three.
findings.assumptions_verified: Multiplicity allowed; all basis choices covered by full eigenspace argument; no simple-spectrum restriction in F.3.
findings.counterevidence: Davies v1 distinguishes weak/strong domains and multiplicity-sensitive upper bounds; those are not universal exact-count existence assertions.
findings.dependency: Bounded background strengthening; not used in new stability or risk derivations.

repair_verification.detail: Delete false existential subclaim. Full nodal theorem restatement still requires weak/strong and multiplicity qualifications.

findings.title: Missing absolute value in signed-filter operator-norm bound
locations: p.7 Section 4.1 first stated stability concern
p.7 Section 4.2 first perturbation inequality and following feature-sensitivity paragraph
findings.claim: Feature term bounded by sup h(lambda) instead of sup |h(lambda)|.
findings.counterexample: K2, L'=L, h=-1, x=(1,0), x'=0: left side1 and printed right side-1. Optional degree2 witness h=-1-lambda^2 and normalized constant x gives same failure.
findings.assumptions_verified: Signed filters allowed; later K>=2 condition does not constrain this earlier general inequality.
findings.dependency: Section 4.1 p.7 announces filter-response size as a stability concern; Section 4.2 p.7 uses the false unsigned bound to derive its main feature-perturbation conclusion. This core dependency supports Major. The separate graph-structure bounds in Theorems 4.2/4.4 and later D.5/4.9/F.6 derivations do not depend on this replacement.

repair_verification.method: Symmetric spectral decomposition; corrected RHS=1 in constant-filter witness

findings.counterevidence: The preceding operator-norm decomposition is valid and makes the intended response-magnitude reading inferable. However, the surrounding maximum-value prose repeats the unsigned quantity and directly uses it for the feature-stability claim. The absolute-value repair remains analytically verified; no empirical-score damage is inferred.

findings.title: Cheeger constant omits the operative cut-domain restriction
findings.claim: lambda2/2<=h<=sqrt(2lambda2) for printed h=min_S cut/(d|S|), with no half-size/volume restriction.
findings.counterexample: Connected unweighted regular K3, d=2, lambda2=3/2. Singletons give ratio1; two-vertex proper sets give1/2. Printed h=1/2<3/4=lambda2/2.
findings.assumptions_verified: Regular graph removes scalar-degree ambiguity; normalized Laplacian; nonempty proper sets adopted as charitable interpretation.
findings.dependency: Local background theorem; not a premise of D.5, 4.9 or F.6.
findings.counterevidence: Conventional volume/min-side definition restores this issue; no claim against standard Cheeger theorem.

repair_verification.statement: Use h_vol=min_{0<vol(S)<=vol(V)/2} cut/vol(S), equivalently divide by min(vol(S),vol(Sbar)).
repair_verification.analytic: Lower Cheeger bound proved by Rayleigh quotient; K3 corrected h=1.
repair_verification.source_checked: Upper Cheeger bound supported by Chung2007 Theorem1; not independently reproved.
